title: Prevent billing drift on service-account alias overlap during staged credential migrations
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Symptom: Over the last three staged credential rotations we observed short windows (30s-2m) of duplicated metering where the same token activity was attributed to both the old and new project bindings. This resulted in immediate billing spikes for affected customers and temporary quota exhaustion for the receiving project.

Hypothesis: During staged migrations we create a new service-account alias and bind it to the target project before revoking the old alias. Due to non-atomic updates across the auth service, proxy routing layer, and the attribution enrichment pipeline, a small fraction of requests are ingested with dual metadata (old_project_id and new_project_id) or with a delayed owner claim update. The usage pipeline currently naively increments counters for every matching claim resulting in double-counting rather than reconciling to a single authoritative owner.

Why this matters: customers experience overcharge and unexpected quota exhaustion; platform dashboards spike and on-call escalations increase. The issue also breaks assumptions in the rate limiter owner attribution which can erroneously throttle the wrong project.

Goals: 
- Prevent future duplicated-attribution windows during credential/alias migrations.
- Backfill and reconcile affected billing windows for impacted customers.
- Add deterministic tests and lightweight runtime checks to detect ambiguous claims in production.

Proposed approach (phased):
1) Short-term mitigation (hotfix): introduce an idempotent "alias-swap" operation in the auth service that performs alias add + remove under a single logical transaction (or sequenced with an atomic tombstone flag). Update proxy to prefer alias-owner with latest-claim-timestamp and ignore claims marked as tombstoned. Deploy within 48 hours.
2) Medium-term (2 sprints): change attribution pipeline to collapse duplicate claims by choosing a single owner per request fingerprint using deterministic tie-breakers (claim timestamp, alias priority table, or last-seen in owner service). Add a dedupe stage before counter increments.
3) Long-term (3+ sprints): unify owner-of-record by extending the metadata propagation protocol — owners must publish final owner version id; ingestion only accepts owner metadata that is consistent with owner-service ledger for the request timestamp. Add migration tooling to atomically rotate aliases with ledger entries.

Acceptance criteria:
- No duplicated billing observed in canary customers during a staged rotation test (simulate noisy traffic).
- Reconciler backfill accurately detects and credits duplicate counts for at least 95% of affected customers from the incident window.
- New unit + e2e tests cover alias-swap and ambiguous-claim scenarios.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Hotfix may slightly delay rotations by a few seconds but avoids customer-facing overcharge.
- Full ledger-style ownership adds complexity to owner-service and needs migration tooling; we'll prototype scope-first.

Observability changes: add a dashboard tile 'ambiguous_attribution_rate' (fraction of requests with >1 valid owner claim), histogram of claim timestamp skew, and per-project retrospective reconciliations. Add an alert when ambiguous rate > 0.1% for >5m.

Backfill plan: run dedupe + attribution pass over raw event windows for the incident periods and produce an adjustments report for billing. Coordinate with Finance/CS for customer credits where confirmed.

2026-02-18 - Liam: Built minimal repro harness and confirmed pipeline increments both counters when ambiguity present. Identified the dedupe insertion point between enrichment and counter-emit stages.

2026-02-22 - Aaron (Platform): Proposed tombstone flag approach for alias-swap. Pros: simple, fast. Cons: requires proxy + ingestion change to respect tombstone state.
2026-02-24 - Liam: Pushed hotfix branch for auth alias-swap semantics (PR #7890). Running unit tests. Need review from Aaron and DevEx before canary deploy.

next_steps: Finish auth hotfix review and deploy to canary cluster; add dedupe stage to metering pipeline PR and run e2e against repro harness; schedule reconciliation run with Finance; document rotation best-practices for SRE/Oncall.
monitoring_playbook:
- After deploy, watch ambiguous_attribution_rate and per-project billing diffs.
- If ambiguous_attribution_rate spikes > 0.05% rollback hotfix.
- Run reconciliation dry-run and validate top-10 customers with largest adjustments before issuing credits.
